rule: Force benchmark: SSB box squat e1RM 1.6-1.75 x bodyweight (treated as about 1.75 x BW back squat).
summary: No normative back-squat-to-bodyweight data for trained, non-powerlifting men were retrieved; the SSB-box to back-squat equivalence is also unsourced. Powerlifting norms show relative squat strength falls by about 0.009-0.013 x BW per kg of body mass, so fixed multipliers suit heavier athletes poorly. Concurrent-training meta-analysis shows that running does not blunt maximal strength gains, so the target need not be lowered for hybrid training. In CrossFit samples back-squat strength explains about 42% of the variance in Fran.

sources.note: Squat multiplier declines 0.0092-0.0125 per kg of body mass across percentiles in male powerlifters.
Schumann 2022: concurrent training does not compromise maximal strength (SMD -0.06) but blunts explosive strength (-0.28), especially in the same session.
Back-squat strength explained 42% of variance in Fran; supports strength mattering for CrossFit, but gives no target.
Strength review: more strength helps general athletic tasks; no specific hybrid threshold.
